title: Tears as Food and Drink
english: They were going and weeping, lifting up their seeds. Coming, they shall arrive in joy, lifting up their gleanings (Ps 126:5). They sow in tears with sweat the seeds of virtue, the seeds of the Spirit, casting them down. When therefore they have harvested, they no longer labor; for they have attained the end of the one striving. When 'going, we were going,' 'we were weeping, lifting up their seeds.' When we were still sowing, having cast down the seed, we were awaiting the perfection of the fruit. When 'we come in joy,' we lift up the gleanings, not yet the seeds. These, therefore, the tears become food for the one desiring to see God and to be gazed upon by Him. Therefore he says: 'My tears became to me bread of days and of night' (Ps 42:3).

I do not weep casually, nor in pleasures, so that at times I might occupy myself with luxury and at times with the weeping of repentance, but also in the dark times; for the dark times are called night. You also have in another psalm a voice saying such a thing: 'You feed us bread of tears and you give me to drink in tears in measure' (Ps 56:8). It is necessary to bring forth the tears of repentance in a measured way, so that they may become bread and drink. And besides, there will be other things that succeed the labor, the offspring produced from the tears.

In that which is said to me every day, 'Where is your God?'; for this reason also I offered so many tears to become food for me, because I heard them saying: 'Where is your God?' (2 Kings 18:33); this also Sennacherib and Rapsakes said: 'Where is the God your God?' And you, Israelite, 'Where is the God your God, that he may save you?' Tears therefore became food for me, but 'in measure,' and I drank them and I ate them; for I knew that the tears and the labor of these things succeed something making joy.

These things I remembered and I poured out upon myself my soul. When in recollection and memory I became of the insults of these ones who were speaking, these my enemies, I did not go out, I did not pour my soul out outside, but upon myself I poured it out. It is such as: 'I was troubled and I did not speak' (Ps 22:14), and what Paul says: 'But we have received the sentence of death within ourselves, so that we may not be trusting in ourselves' (2 Cor 4:8). This also is said concerning Job: previously he says that 'Job did not sin,' and secondly: 'with the lips.'
the intellect

title: Thanksgiving as Confession of Wonders
english: Of confession: there is no lamentation when the passage and haste toward the house of God occurs, but rather a rejoicing. For Abraham thus 'rejoiced in order to see my day, and having seen, he rejoiced' (John 8:51). He saw the day of the Lord by arriving into his house, into perfect faith.

The name of confession in the Scriptures signifies two things, so that I may not say a third meaning. The public disclosure regarding sins is called confession, as if one says: 'having been gathered to confess concerning your sins.' This is found in the Epistle of Barnabas, in the epistle according to him: 'having been gathered to confess concerning your sins.' And again: 'confess your sins to one another' (James 5:16). 'I made my sin known to you, and my lawlessness I did not cover; I said, I will disclose my lawlessness to myself before the Lord' (Psalm 32:5). One confesses while wailing and stripping off his former sins.

It also signifies thanksgiving, as if the Savior says: 'I will confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden the divine things from the wise and understanding, and have revealed them to infants' (Matthew 11:25). He does not give thanks for the fact that 'the divine things are hidden from the wise and understanding,' but for the fact that those who are infants have been enabled to see them revealed. These are the ones from the Gentiles who have believed, whereas the wise and the understanding, from whom the divine things are hidden, are those of the circumcision.

[Fragmentary] He cried this out: 'How do you say, We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us? For in vain you were born...' [Fragmentary] 'The wise were shamed and called upon, because they rejected the word of the Lord.' Since they themselves rejected it, the Scripture became in vain to them. For because of the... [Fragmentary] It is said that, when the letters were first being taken, they were found in small scraps; again, they did it with tablets. And since they understood that those written on tablets... [Fragmentary] so that they might have various tools for writing these things. Therefore, 'the wise were shamed and were deceived, because they rejected the word of the Lord; what kind of wisdom is in them?' For how... [Fragmentary] those who reject...

How do you hear the word of the Lord? Thanksgiving, therefore, is manifested through confession. And: 'Let us confess to you, O God; let us confess to you, all peoples. I will recount all your wonders when I take my portion' (Ps 105:45). The one who confesses by recounting the wonders is praising [God], not regarding his own sins.

And again: 'I will confess to you, Lord, with all my heart; I will recount all your wonders; I shall be glad and shall rejoice in you' (Ps 9:1). And a third time this is said: often the harmony and the [thing] joined... 'I will clothe myself in confession and majesty' (Ps 32:1). There is nothing in you... that of virtue which envies your majesty. And again: 'Confession and beauty before him' (Ps 32:1).

Again here the harmony... you do not take confession here as the disclosure of sins... remaining in harmony. The voice of those celebrating this is... having become [it] by voice, but their cry is this: to confess... 'The voice of rejoicing and confession, the tabernacles of the righteous' (Ps 135:4); in those making progress, 'the voice of rejoicing and confession' is, for they were freed from wickedness.

And it is also possible that 'in the tabernacles of the righteous'... when they look up at them and enslave them, when the temples of him... 'Why are you dejected, my soul, and why are you disturbed?' (Ps 42:5)... until someone reaches the house of God. And you, O soul, having remembered... and saying: 'Where is your God?' do not be dejected, do not be disturbed... become. You are able also to receive the angels who are 'celebrating'... 'but you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the festival of myriads of angels' (Heb 12:22). 'Why are you dejected and why are you disturbed?' title: The Light of the Face and the Inner Disturbance
english: Helping. As if even while laboring you say, and while sick: 'Why have you despaired of health? Behold, the physician is present.' Hope in God, because I will confess to him; salvation of my face and my God. God is present; expect from him to be freed from sorrow and trouble. Then he was freed from these, when the sorrows reached an end, when... for he removes the trouble, he removes the sorrow.

'Salvation of my face.' We say regarding 'the eyes of the wise are in his head,' because in the... and the prudent and the imprudent have their faces. 'Salvation...' is said in the scripture regarding the face, which is often said, not regarding... 'May the Lord lift up his face upon you and give you peace' (Num 6:26); for not face... 'May the Lord make his face shine upon you and bless you' (Num 6:25). Here the face that appears... it is also said 'image of the invisible God,' the 'character of his substance' (Col 1:15); salvation and blessing follow, if this face is lifted up and becomes unmixed.

What then is the face? —that which the man took up... a snatching up as if it is the face of God, it is made known... I once also explained into that by a second implication... the Son says the form of the Father, form as his character or form as they construct an idea in the soul. Therefore, salvation is of my face. Having become... it is not that of the body, but regarding that which is said... for it does not say this, that the face of the body without a covering...

Where the face is revealed from ignorance and sin; for 'the wisdom of man brightens his face' (Proverbs 15:30). This bright face does not have a covering of ignorance, nor an overlay of wickedness, but is pure; you are the salvation of the face, O God.

My soul was disturbed toward myself; [this is] the kind of disturbance. And this was also said, when he says, 'I poured out my soul upon myself' (Psalm 62:8) toward the outside; I did not appear to them being disordered. The one being disturbed by these things, his disturbance is turned toward himself.

Therefore I will remember you from the land of Jordan and Hermon (Psalm 133:3). Since my soul is disturbed, even if the disturbance is toward myself, I need a cleansing bath, I have need of baptism. 'I remembered you' therefore 'from the land of Jordan and Hermon'. Hermon is interpreted as 'way of the lamp' or 'offering'. This says that this mountain... acting meteorically, having a divided mind, being illuminated, makes the traveler go straight. And Jordan is interpreted as 'their descent'. It is able to descend, but for their sake it descended, just as an excellent teacher... from a small mountain, the abyss calls to abyss into the voice of your cataracts.

It is, and it is manifest; for 'the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, and let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord' (Psalm 20:6). Even if it is toward us and toward creation, what is being judged together with us. And I say: the Word of God, the God Word, becomes toward each of the prophets; for 'those he called gods, to whom the word of God came' (Psalm 82:6). 'The word of the Lord came to me, saying' (Jeremiah 1:4). If then toward those who are made gods...
